items.stem: What is the main purpose of the Define phase in design thinking?

options.text: To frame a clear, user-centred problem statement to solve
options.rationale: Correct: Define synthesises research into an actionable problem framing.
That is far later; Define precedes ideation.

Marketing is outside the design-thinking cycle here.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make a prototype useful for learning early? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep it low-fidelity so it is fast and cheap to change
options.rationale: Correct: low fidelity lets you iterate before over-investing.

options.text: Test it with real users and observe their behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: real user testing reveals what actually works.

options.text: Perfect every visual detail before showing anyone
options.rationale: Polish slows learning and discourages change.

options.text: Only ask users whether they like it

items.explanation: Correct: low fidelity plus real user testing accelerates learning.

items.stem: During a brainstorm, a team keeps critiquing ideas as they are suggested. Why is this a problem?

options.text: Early judgement suppresses the volume and range of ideas
options.rationale: Correct: divergent thinking needs judgement deferred to generate options.

options.text: Critique is never useful in design thinking
options.rationale: Critique is valuable later, in the converging step.

options.text: It makes the session too long
options.rationale: The issue is idea suppression, not length.
The phase is ideation; the problem is premature judgement.

items.explanation: Correct: divergent thinking needs judgement deferred to generate options.
